title: Lesson 03 – System Documentation Techniques Part 1
description: Examines system documentation methods including data flow diagrams, flowcharts, and business process diagrams used to analyze and design information systems.
subject: ACC2475 - Accounting Information Systems and ERP Applications

questions.question: Which situation most clearly demonstrates the primary purpose of system documentation in an organization?
options: Replacing employee training programs with automated instructions
Providing a structured explanation of how data moves and is processed within a system
Eliminating the need for internal controls in transaction processing
Reducing the requirement for communication between departments
questions.answer: Providing a structured explanation of how data moves and is processed within a system
questions.rationale: Documentation explains how systems function including inputs, processing, storage, outputs, and controls.

questions.question: An analyst reviews diagrams showing the origins, movement, transformation, and storage of data within a payroll system. Which documentation technique is primarily being used?
questions.answer: Data flow diagram
questions.rationale: Data flow diagrams show where data originates, how it moves, how it is transformed, and where it is stored.

questions.question: Which documentation tool is most appropriate when the objective is to illustrate how physical documents move between departments?
questions.answer: Document flowchart
questions.rationale: Document flowcharts describe the flow of documents and information between organizational units.

questions.question: Which characteristic distinguishes a system flowchart from a document flowchart?
options: It focuses on logical processing steps rather than document movement
It describes the physical movement of printed documents
It focuses only on employee responsibilities
questions.answer: It focuses on logical processing steps rather than document movement
questions.rationale: System flowcharts show relationships among inputs, processing, and outputs within a system.

questions.question: A program flowchart primarily documents which aspect of a system?
options: The movement of documents between departments
The logical sequence of operations within a computer program
The organizational reporting structure of employees
The external entities interacting with a system
questions.answer: The logical sequence of operations within a computer program
questions.rationale: Program flowcharts describe the sequence of logical operations performed by software.

questions.question: In a data flow diagram, which element represents an organization or individual that sends or receives data?
questions.answer: Data source or destination
questions.rationale: External entities that send or receive data are represented as sources or destinations.

questions.question: In a data flow diagram, arrows primarily represent which concept?
questions.answer: Movement of data between elements
questions.rationale: Arrows represent the flow of data between processes, stores, and external entities.

questions.question: Which DFD element represents the transformation of incoming data into outgoing information?
questions.answer: Transformation process
questions.rationale: Processes transform input data into output information within a system.

questions.question: Which DFD component represents a temporary or permanent repository of data?
questions.answer: Data store
questions.rationale: Data stores represent files or databases where data are stored.

questions.question: Why must every transformation process in a DFD have both input and output data flows?
options: To ensure that each process actually transforms incoming data into new outputs
To ensure diagrams maintain symmetrical layouts
To allow processes to store permanent data records
To reduce the number of external entities shown
questions.answer: To ensure that each process actually transforms incoming data into new outputs
questions.rationale: Processes must receive input data and produce output data to represent meaningful transformations.

questions.question: When two related data elements always move together through a system, how should they appear in a DFD?
options: Combined as a single labeled data flow
questions.answer: Combined as a single labeled data flow
questions.rationale: Data elements that always flow together are represented using a single data flow line.

questions.question: Which diagram represents the highest level overview of a system within a data flow diagram hierarchy?
questions.answer: Context diagram
questions.rationale: A context diagram provides a summary view of the system and its external entities.

questions.question: Why are complex data flow diagrams subdivided into lower levels?
options: To simplify diagrams and provide increasing levels of detail
To eliminate the need for context diagrams
To reduce the number of external entities
To convert diagrams into program code
questions.answer: To simplify diagrams and provide increasing levels of detail
questions.rationale: Large systems require multiple levels of DFDs to present detailed information clearly.

questions.question: Which guideline recommends identifying system boundaries before constructing a DFD?
options: Determine system scope and included data elements
Combine all flows into one diagram
questions.answer: Determine system scope and included data elements
questions.rationale: System boundaries determine what elements are included or excluded from the diagram.

questions.question: Which documentation component describes the meaning and structure of every data element used in a system?
questions.answer: Data dictionary
questions.rationale: A data dictionary defines and documents all data elements, flows, and stores.

questions.question: Which guideline emphasizes naming data flows first when designing a DFD?
options: To ensure attention focuses on the movement of data rather than system structure
To eliminate the need for data stores
To ensure processes are drawn before entities
To standardize diagram layout across departments
questions.answer: To ensure attention focuses on the movement of data rather than system structure
questions.rationale: Focusing on data flows first helps analysts understand system data movement clearly.

questions.question: Why should unrelated processes not be combined into a single transformation process in a DFD?
options: Because unrelated processes distort the logical structure of data transformations
Because multiple processes require separate software systems
Because it increases the number of external entities
Because it eliminates the need for data stores
questions.answer: Because unrelated processes distort the logical structure of data transformations
questions.rationale: Combining unrelated activities obscures the logical flow of data and system functions.

questions.question: Which guideline recommends limiting each DFD page to approximately five to seven processes?
options: To maintain readability and prevent diagram complexity
To eliminate the need for data dictionaries
To ensure processes are identical in structure
questions.answer: To maintain readability and prevent diagram complexity
questions.rationale: Too many processes reduce readability and clarity of diagrams.

questions.question: Why are physical storage details such as alphabetical file organization typically excluded from DFDs?
options: Because DFDs focus on logical data flows rather than physical storage methods
Because physical storage information is confidential
Because physical storage has no impact on system design
Because storage methods are only shown in program flowcharts
questions.answer: Because DFDs focus on logical data flows rather than physical storage methods
questions.rationale: DFDs illustrate logical data movement rather than physical implementation details.

questions.question: Which principle recommends organizing DFDs so that data generally flows from top to bottom and from left to right?
questions.answer: Data flow orientation guideline
questions.rationale: Clear directional organization improves readability and interpretation of diagrams.

questions.question: Which situation best demonstrates the practical value of system documentation for internal control evaluation?
options: Managers analyzing diagrams to detect weaknesses in transaction authorization procedures
Auditors ignoring documentation during system reviews
Managers relying exclusively on verbal explanations
questions.answer: Managers analyzing diagrams to detect weaknesses in transaction authorization procedures
questions.rationale: Documentation helps evaluate system controls and identify weaknesses.

questions.question: In a data flow diagram, [dropdown_1] represent transformations of data, while [dropdown_2] represent repositories where data are stored.
questions.rationale: Processes transform data while data stores represent storage locations.

questions.question: The [dropdown_1] diagram provides the highest level overview of a system, while lower level diagrams provide increasing levels of [dropdown_2].
questions.rationale: Context diagrams summarize the system while lower levels provide greater detail.

questions.question: In DFD notation, data sources and destinations are typically represented by [dropdown_1], while data flows are represented by [dropdown_2].
questions.rationale: Squares represent external entities and arrows represent data movement.

questions.question: A diagram that graphically illustrates how data move through a system is called a ________.
questions.answer: data flow diagram
questions.rationale: Data flow diagrams show the movement and transformation of data.

questions.question: A repository where data are stored temporarily or permanently in a DFD is called a ________.
questions.answer: data store
questions.rationale: Data stores represent locations where data are held for later use.

questions.question: A structured list describing every data element, store, and flow in a system is known as a ________.
questions.answer: data dictionary
questions.rationale: The data dictionary defines all system data components.

questions.question: Which elements are fundamental components of a data flow diagram?
questions.rationale: These four elements form the basic structure of a DFD.

questions.question: Which objectives can system documentation help achieve within an organization?
options: Evaluating internal controls and identifying weaknesses
Designing new systems or improving existing systems
Replacing the need for system users
answer: Evaluating internal controls and identifying weaknesses
Designing new systems or improving existing systems
questions.rationale: Documentation helps understand, evaluate, and design systems.

questions.question: Which guidelines should be followed when designing a clear and effective data flow diagram?
options: Identify system boundaries before designing the diagram
Use descriptive names for data flows and processes
Ignore all data inputs entering the system
answer: Identify system boundaries before designing the diagram
Use descriptive names for data flows and processes
questions.rationale: These guidelines help maintain clarity and logical accuracy in DFDs.
